title: Canonical unbounded derived adjunction comparisons on arbitrary sheaf slices
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by sites small in the chosen universe, with commutative coefficient rings and a structural map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Let $A$ be any sheaf of sets on the target, put $B=f^{-1}A$, and present the slices $\mathscr Y/A$ and $\mathscr X/B$ by the small element sites of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. Write $R_{Y,A}$ and $R_{X,B}$ for the restricted rings and $r_Y,r_X$ for exact module restriction to these slices. There is a canonical ringed morphism $f_A:(\mathscr X/B,R_{X,B})\to(\mathscr Y/A,R_{Y,A})$ whose inverse image sends $(H\to A)$ to $(f^{-1}H\to B)$. Its ordinary module pullback and direct image satisfy $\sigma:f_A^*r_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}r_Xf^*$ and $r_Yf_*\cong f_{A*}r_X$.
Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical K-flat pullbacks and K-injective direct images with their derived adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Exact restriction induces functors, denoted again by $r_X,r_Y$, on these derived categories. For every $M\in D(R_Y)$ and $E\in D(R_X)$ there are natural isomorphisms
$$\theta_M:Lf_A^*r_YM\xrightarrow{\sim}r_XLf^*M,\qquad
\beta_E:r_YRf_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{A*}r_XE.$$
Here $\theta$ is the canonical derived pullback comparison induced by the commutative ringed slice square: on a K-flat complex $T$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] it is the image of $\sigma_T$ in the derived category, under the canonical representative identifications. Restriction of $T$ remains K-flat with flat terms. The map $\beta_E$ is represented, on a K-injective representative $I$ of $E$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], by the ordinary restriction/direct-image identity $r_Yf_*I\cong f_{A*}r_XI$; $r_XI$ is K-injective. Moreover $\beta$ is the adjunction exchange mate of $\theta$. In particular, for the canonical counits $\varepsilon$ of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and $\varepsilon^A$ of $Lf_A^*\dashv Rf_{A*}$,
$$r_X(\varepsilon_E)\circ\theta_{Rf_*E}
=\varepsilon^A_{r_XE}\circ Lf_A^*(\beta_E).$$
No presentation of $f$ by a functor between the original sites, no flatness or invertibility of $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$, and no boundedness assumption on the complexes is required.
